entries.brief: ONE compact UNRIGGED WOODEN NAVAL DESIGN MODEL of an eighteenth-century sailing warship hull, inspired broadly by Navy Board models. The whole recognizable hull is present, not merely a fragment of ribs: continuous central keel, rounded full bow, squared raised stern, and a series of coherent transverse U-shaped oak frames that attach to the same keel and follow the curved hull shape. Part of the hull near the stern is planked in honey-brown wood; the forward portion is deliberately cut away to reveal frames, deck beams and two simple internal deck levels. No random disconnected posts, impossible braces, floating timbers or broken joins. No diagonal strengthening timbers: this represents design study, not the already illustrated diagonal framing technology. Entire model without masts, sails, rigging, cannon or elaborate gilded carving, occupying most of a compact square on a diagonal. One large functional brass DRAFTING DIVIDER rests immediately against the model, slightly open, two straight hinged legs ending in sharp metal points, clearly subordinate and proportionate to a small study model. No plinth, mounting board, labels, ocean, shipyard, ground, construction workers or scattered drawings. Warm natural oak grain, dark inner frames, restrained brass highlights. This is a stylized conceptual design model, not a certified reconstruction of a named vessel.

entries.brief: ONE thick OPEN SHIP INSPECTION REGISTER of the late eighteenth century, viewed obliquely from above. A worn deep muted olive-green leather binding, simple brown leather spine, cream paper block and clearly coherent central book gutter. On the left facing page, ONE LARGE simple ink profile diagram of a period sailing merchant ship with three masts, no detailed rigging, no words or annotations. On the right facing page, a clean inspection table with a few broad ruled rows and columns ONLY, no scribbles, pseudo-text, letters, numerals, seals or stamps. Keep the diagram and grid bold enough to read as ship records rather than a map or ordinary novel. The single supporting accessory is ONE period brass-and-steel OUTSIDE MEASURING CALIPER lying partly across the lower edge of the open book: two coherent curved jaws joined at one pivot, a modest opening, no sharp divider points, no watch or compass. The caliper signifies physical inspection, not nautical navigation. Natural cream pages, subdued olive leather, muted brass, black ink, no uniform brown/gold wash. No coin purse, money, modern clipboard, fountain pen, magnifying glass, additional papers, logos, certificates, invented official badge or actual copied Lloyd's cover. This is a symbolic interpretation of vessel registration and inspection, not a reproduction of an actual register page.

entries.brief: ONE recognizable EARLY ROWING RESCUE LIFEBOAT, inspired by Henry Greathead-type boats circa 1790-1810, isolated in elevated three-quarter view. A broad deep curved DOUBLE-ENDED wooden clinker-planked hull with both pointed ends raised and an open interior, sturdy warm oak ribs, five broad crosswise wooden seating thwarts, no square transom. A thick tan CORK BUOYANCY BAND wraps continuously around the exterior just below the gunwale, and cork blocks are visible beneath the inner side edges of the seating. Make the cork band prominent, coarse-grained and clearly distinct from the dark brown planked hull; this is the distinguishing lifesaving feature. Exactly TWO long simple wooden OARS form one subordinate accessory pair, laid parallel lengthwise over the seating, with coherent straight shafts and broad paddle blades, fully within the compact group. No mast, sails, anchor, engine, motorboat cabin, modern orange inflatable, white-red plastic lifebuoy, lifejacket, helmet, people, injured person, water, waves or landscape. No model mounting stand or wheeled launching carriage. The open interior, raised double ends and cork protection must remain clear at small size. Natural dark honey-brown wood, tan cork and muted iron fastenings, not a blue-white modern boat. This is a stylized concept of organized maritime rescue, not an exact artifact copy.
